title: Enabling innovation in the world of venture capital

turns.speaker: Guest Speaker 1
turns.text: A lot of the enabling infrastructure to start a venture fund, primarily driven by the work that Angelus is doing, is now far more accessible. So it's easier to start smaller funds. Specifically, Angelus has a product called rolling funds

turns.speaker: Guest Speaker 1
turns.text: you can get LPs to subscribe to your fund on a quarter by quarter basis. What traditionally used to happen

turns.speaker: Guest Speaker 1
turns.text: you needed to raise from LPs and have this big bang

turns.speaker: Guest Speaker 1
turns.text: Event, it's much harder to do that if you don't have a track record. And the kind of cold start problem always was,

turns.speaker: Guest Speaker 1
turns.text: LPs don't want to invest in you because you don't have a track record. And then how do you build a track record? If you don't have enough personal capital to angel invest, if you're not a scout

turns.speaker: Guest Speaker 1
turns.text: actually prove to LPs, right, that you actually do have good access

turns.speaker: Guest Speaker 1
turns.text: can be like a high performing investor. So rolling funds, I think to an extent actually solves that problem. It's really important enabling innovation.
